newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec insurance deadline won't be extended - Shapiro.
newsitem.headline: Dec insurance deadline won't be extended - Shapiro.

text.p: A December 15 deadline to settle a U.S.-Japan dispute over deregulation of Japan's insurance market will not be extended, senior U.S. Trade Representative negotiator Ira Shapiro told reporters on Tuesday.
Shapiro, speaking after a day and a half of talks here on the dispute, said no progress had been made on resolving major issues and the two sides remained "a considerable distance apart".
He said: "The issues will require ministerial attention and discussion and they will get it."
Shapiro also said a meeting between Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, set for December 6 and 7, would be "hopefully determinative".

Asked about the possibility of U.S. trade sanctions should no agreement be reached, Shapiro said: "We have said we have to resolve the dispute by December 15 and that we will respond appropriately to things that happen after that if we have not been able to reach an agreement."

Asked if Barshefsky and Mitsuzuka might meet again if they should fail to forge a deal on December 6 and 7, Shapiro said: "We are focused on this meeting, and I think this is the meeting at which the ministers will make their efforts to resolve the major issues."
He said Japan's deregulation of its automotive insurance sector was very important, as was deregulation of the primary life and non-life sectors overall.
Japan and the United States are at odds over the implementation of a 1994 bilateral agreement to open Japan's $382 billion insurance market.

Washington has accused Tokyo of reneging on the agreement by moving to deregulate its "third sector" niche insurance market -- for such cover as personal accident and health care insurance -- in which foreign firms have a strong foothold, before opening its primary life and casualty markets.

A senior Ministry of Finance official, briefing reporters on the meeting between Shapiro and Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, said if Mitsuzuka and Barshefsky did not settle the issue on December 6 and 7, there was almost no chance of them meeting again before the deadline.
